transcript.text: Hi, my Bosch WAN28281GB has stopped half way through a wash and is showing E18. Water still in the drum. What does that mean?

E18 means the machine has not drained within the allowed time. With water still in the drum, this is a drainage fault rather than a spin fault. Most often it is a blocked pump filter/coin trap or an item caught just behind it; a kinked or blocked drain hose is next. The drain pump itself is possible, but do not assume it needs replacing until the simple blockages are ruled out. 1. Switch off at the socket and unplug it. Put towels and a shallow tray down at the lower front flap. If there is a small emergency drain tube, use that first; otherwise loosen the pump filter very gradually, pausing to empty the tray. There can be a lot of water.
2. Remove and clean the filter. Look for coins, hair grips, buttons, lint or fabric. With the filter out, use a torch and gently check whether the small impeller behind it is clear and can move; do not force it. A trapped object is often the fix.
3. Check the drain hose behind the machine is not kinked, squashed or pushed too far into a blocked standpipe/sink waste. A restriction here can give exactly the same E18. If the filter and hose are clear but it still will not drain, run a drain/spin programme and listen near the bottom front: a hum with no water leaving suggests a jammed/weak pump or a deeper blockage; complete silence can indicate the pump or its electrical supply and is usually an engineer job. Do not open the filter quickly while the drum is full, as water can flood out.
Thanks, I'll give that a go. I've unplugged it and will start with the emergency drain tube and then the filter. There's a hum from low down at the front when it tries to drain, and no burning smell.

A failed or jammed pump remains possible, but do not replace it unless those blockages are ruled out. 1. Continue with the emergency drain tube first, using towels and a shallow tray. Keep the machine unplugged.
2. Remove the filter and clear anything found. Then shine a torch into the opening and gently feel whether the small impeller can move. It may turn in small steps rather than spin freely; it should not be solidly jammed. Do not force it. - Debris or an item caught there: clear it, refit the filter firmly and test a drain/spin cycle. - Filter clear but impeller jammed, rough or visibly broken: the pump is more likely to need an engineer/replacement.
3. If the filter and impeller are clear, check the external drain hose is not kinked or crushed, and that the standpipe/sink waste is not blocked. A humming pump with no discharge can also be a blocked hose or household waste pipe. No burning smell is reassuring, but it does not distinguish a blockage from a weak pump. Tell me what you find at the filter/impeller and we can decide the sensible next step.

I've emptied the water with the emergency tube (took several trays) and unscrewed the filter. There was a child's sock and a hair grip wrapped round it, plus a lot of fluff. I got a little water on the floor while doing it. The impeller turns, slightly notchy at first and then free. What should I do next?

The sock, hair grip and fluff are a very convincing cause of the E18. The slight notchiness followed by free movement can be normal for a pump impeller; it is not enough on its own to condemn the pump. 1. Wipe the filter opening and the filter’s rubber seal clean, then screw the filter back in straight and fully hand-tight. This matters because water can leak if the seal is trapped or the cap is cross-threaded.
2. Dry the floor, plug the machine back in, and run a drain/spin programme with the machine empty. Stay nearby for the first minute and check around the filter flap for any drip. If it drains fully and no E18 returns, the blockage was the fault and it is resolved. The little water spilled while emptying it is normal during this job. If it still hums but does not discharge water, check the external drain hose and the standpipe/sink waste for a kink or blockage. If those are clear, the remaining likely cause is the drain pump or a deeper obstruction in the sump hose, which is best dealt with by an engineer.
Thanks, I've refitted the filter and run the drain and spin programme. It drained quickly, E18 has gone and it spun normally. No drips that I could see. Is there anything else I should do?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. No further repair is needed. The sock, hair grip and fluff were blocking the drain path; the quick drain, cleared E18 and normal spin confirm it is resolved. For prevention, check and clean the pump filter periodically—particularly after washing children’s items, and check pockets for small objects. If E18 returns soon despite the filter remaining clear, then check the drain hose/waste connection or arrange an engineer visit; but on the result of this test, the pump itself is working normally.

candidates: Blocked pump filter or foreign object in the pump path (high)
Kinked or blocked drain hose/waste connection (medium)
